title: sdks: unify auth/retries and streaming ergonomics across python/ts/go + v1.26.0 bumps
author: Ava Chen
body: Summary: This PR unifies auth and retry behaviors and normalizes streaming ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: We have multiple inconsistencies between SDKs for token refresh behavior, retry backoff defaults, and the streaming callback/async ergonomics which cause customer confusion and customer-reported issues when migrating between languages. This change set: 1) Introduces a shared auth adapter pattern and consistent default retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 5 retries for idempotent calls, 1 retry for non-idempotent by default) across SDKs. 2) Adds a stable streaming client surface: async iterator for Python, AsyncIterator/ReadableStream-compatible wrapper in TypeScript, and channel-based consumer pattern in Go with clear cancellation semantics. 3) Updates docs and examples for streaming and auth best practices. 4) Bumps SDK versions: python v1.26.0, typescript v1.26.0, go v1.26.0 and updates changelogs. 5) Adds cross-language integration tests and small runtime fixes discovered during testing. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1423) referenced - [x] Cross-language tests added - [x] Docs updated - [x] Release notes drafted - [x] All CI green except one flaky integration job rerun and passed Context and compatibility: Default behaviors remain backward-compatible for existing users; opt-in flags are provided for devs who need old retry semantics. For customers relying on very custom retry policies we expose a RetryPolicy interface and helper builders in each SDK. Rollout plan: merge to main, publish SDKs behind the normal release pipeline with feature-flagged server behavior for 2 weeks to monitor client telemetry for unexpected error spikes. Related: PRs to examples and quickstarts will follow in a separate changelist.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) please add a short note in the python docs about coroutine cancellation semantics and GC interaction, (2) could we centralize the jitter function to a shared util to avoid small divergence later?
Ava Chen (author): Thanks Diego, added the note to docs and moved jitter to shared/utils in this PR (see commit d4e5f6g).

Priya Rao: Verified behavior in local integration tests. Minor: TypeScript ReadableStream wrapper needs explicit backpressure propagation when downstream closes - added a suggested patch in the review thread.
Ethan Liu: Go streaming looks clean. Please add one more unit test around canceled context edge case. I ran the stress harness; saw no memory growth after 30m.
Ava Chen (author): Addressed Priya and Ethan's comments: added TS backpressure handling and a Go unit test for canceled contexts. CI reran and passed.
Priya Rao: Approving now. Will coordinate release notes with docs team.
release_notes:
- SDKs: Unified auth adapter and default retry policy across Python/TypeScript/Go.
- Streaming: Stable, ergonomic streaming surfaces per language (Python async iterator, TypeScript ReadableStream wrapper, Go channel pattern).
- Version bumps: python/typescript/go v1.26.0.
- Docs: Updated streaming and auth best-practices.
notes_for_qa: Smoke test streaming examples in all three SDKs, verify token refresh and retry behavior by simulating transient 5xx and 401-with-refresh scenarios, and validate no regression in latency-sensitive paths.
post_merge_tasks: Publish packages to registries, monitor client telemetry for increased error rates, follow-up PR to update quickstarts and examples repository.
